messages:
Anya T: Heads-up: canary for nf4+fp4 rolled last night is showing a throughput drop ~25% and a memory thump on kernels with small batches. p95 up 3x. Logs attached in thread.
Matt R: ugh. Observed similar on 4 hosts in scalepool-eu. Kernel selector keeps oscillating between quant4_small and quant4_large which looks suspicious.
Sasha: can you paste the selector decisions from telemetry? suspect heuristic weight for 'seq_len_hist' flipped after latest profiling.
Anya T: telemetry snippet:
```json
{"host":"eu-r1-23","selector_path":["quant4_small","quant4_large","quant4_small"],"kv_cache_mb":2300,"alloc_fail":false}
```
Also seeing host with memory spike to 7.2GB beyond expected. p99 latency heatmap attached.
Kevin: quick repro steps I used:
```
curl -s -X POST https://canary-api.redwood/run -d @payload.json
perf record -g -p <pid> -- sleep 10
```
I reproduced kernel hop and then background prefetcher triggered thrash.
runtime-bot: Deployment nf4-fp4-canary/2026-03-17T03:12 by matt.r succeeded; autoscaler triggered scale-up at 03:40.
Matt R: suspect change is the batching heuristic that increases prefill for sequences <32; that interacts badly with quant4_small's slab allocator. Reverting heuristic locally removes the thump.
Sasha: can we try toggling 'prefetch_v2' off for canary and run the 1-hour soak? @kevin can you enable a metric that logs kernel_max_frag_mb?
Kevin: toggled prefetch_v2=false on canary hosts, kicking soak now. Added metric kernel_max_frag_mb (sampling: 5s). Will report in 30m. :crossed_fingers: 
Anya T: thanks — also adding a small eval to check quality impact of prefetched batches; if we degrade accuracy we stop.
Matt R: if soak is clean, follow-up: update selector to prefer quant4_large for bursty small batches until allocator PR lands. I'll open a patch.
Sasha: filing an incident note in incidents/ with initial findings. assigning to @matt.r for follow-up.
Kevin: soak 18m in — memory spikes stopped on first two hosts. kernel_max_frag_mb went from 4200 -> 1200. Tentative win.
Anya T: great. leave the canary running; we'll decide on rollback only if p95 stays > target for 1h. Thanks all :rocket:
